# Tenhaw Kit

Local-first agent tools for AI readiness, delivery performance, AI business cases, use-case registers and operating models. MIT code, CC BY 4.0 framework content. No installed-tool telemetry.

Published release: 1.0.1, verified 2026-11-16. [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tenhaw/v/1.0.1), [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tenhaw/1.0.1/), [official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/com.tenhaw%2Fkit/versions/1.0.1), identity com.tenhaw/kit. Core tools require no Tenhaw API key.

## Install

```sh
npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 --help
codex mcp add tenhaw -- npx -y @tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1
uvx --from tenhaw==1.0.1 tenhaw-py --help
```

Remote MCP: https://mcp.tenhaw.com/mcp . Local: eight tools. Remote: six pure tools, aggregate delivery metrics only.

## One prompt for a coding agent

Install Tenhaw Kit 1.0.1 for this project and continue my requested task. Identify the coding client and use its documented project MCP configuration with npx -y @tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1. Preserve existing servers and instructions; report conflicting Tenhaw definitions for review. Verify the expected eight local tools and a synthetic readiness calculation. If I request a starter, scaffold a new directory, install its dependencies and run its documented build and tests. Ask me to set only missing local environment variables required for GitHub or Jira collection I request. Keep secret values out of chat, command arguments, configuration and logs. Report the checks that passed and any remaining host reload or trust step.

## Automated setup from source

The setup command is unreleased and is not included in npm 1.0.1. Build the source checkout, then run:

```sh
node packages/cli/dist/index.js setup --agent codex --directory /path/to/project --json
```

Setup plans by default. Add --yes to apply, --check to inspect without writing, and --verify to probe the selected MCP server with a synthetic readiness calculation. Agents: codex, claude, cursor, vscode, gemini. Defaults: --transport local --integration none. GitHub/Jira collection requires local transport and only the relevant environment credentials. Report missing variable names, never values. Confirm the tool call inside the selected client after its reload or trust step. [Full agent install guide](https://github.com/Tenhaw/tenhaw-kit/blob/main/docs/AGENT_INSTALL.md).

## Focused app source previews

Six hosted product profiles and one desktop developer package are implemented in source. Directory submission and publication are separate owner operations. [Catalogue](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/), [machine-readable products](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps.json).

- Tenhaw AI Business Case: Build an AI business case from your explicit operating and cost assumptions. Compare low, base and high scenarios, recovered capacity, cash flow, NPV and payback. Explore editable project-cost assumptions. Results support planning; they are not a quote or financial advice. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/business-case/).
- Tenhaw AI Readiness: Run an evidence-led AI readiness self-assessment using 30 anchored questions across six dimensions. See scores, response coverage and gaps. Maturity bands require at least 80% response coverage. This supports internal self-assessment, not certification. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/readiness/).
- Tenhaw Use-case Prioritiser: Prioritise supplied AI use cases using explicit value, feasibility, ownership and indicative governance gates. Inspect dependencies and outcome measures before taking an idea forward. The app does not certify legal risk or approve deployment. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/usecase-prioritiser/).
- Tenhaw Delivery Health: Review one service's delivery health from a supplied aggregate metrics report. Keep reporting windows, sample sizes and unavailable observations visible. The hosted app accepts aggregate metrics only; it does not collect repository events or rank unrelated teams. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/delivery-health/).
- Tenhaw Operating Model: Connect supplied teams, OKRs, roadmap outcomes and interactions into an explainable product operating model. Inspect missing ownership and dependency checks. The app supports organisational design conversations; it does not prescribe a reorganisation or fabricate team commitments. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/operating-model/).
- Tenhaw AI Procurement: Prepare a vendor-neutral AI procurement pack from a defined buying brief. Select evidence questions, must-have criteria and blank supplier response worksheets. Sector prompts support the buyer's own review. No supplier claims, prices, rankings, legal advice or procurement approval are invented. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/procurement/).
- Tenhaw Kit Developer Tools: Build internal product tools with connected deterministic calculations and local coding workflows. Validate readiness, aggregate delivery evidence, AI business cases, use-case registers and operating models through one remote MCP connection; scaffold projects and integrate the results locally. Desktop execution is required for local work. [Source preview](https://kit.tenhaw.com/apps/developer-kit/).

## Agent installation

### claude

Project configuration: .mcp.json.

claude mcp add --scope project tenhaw -- npx -y @tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1

### codex

Project configuration: .codex/config.toml.

codex mcp add tenhaw -- npx -y @tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1

### gemini

Project configuration: .gemini/settings.json.

gemini extensions install https://github.com/Tenhaw/tenhaw-gemini

### cursor

Project configuration: .cursor/mcp.json.

{"mcpServers":{"tenhaw":{"command":"npx","args":["-y","@tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1"]}}}

### vscode

Project configuration: .mcp.json.

{"mcpServers":{"tenhaw":{"type":"stdio","command":"npx","args":["-y","@tenhaw/mcp@1.0.1"],"tools":["*"]}}}

[Add to Cursor](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=tenhaw&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoibnB4IiwiYXJncyI6WyIteSIsIkB0ZW5oYXcvbWNwQDEuMC4xIl19)

## AI readiness assessment

When to use: Assess organisational AI readiness from evidence-backed answers across six dimensions.

Install: npm install @tenhaw/ai-readiness@1.0.1

CLI: npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 readiness --input answers.json --json

API: scoreReadiness({ answers: [{ questionId: 'strategy-1', score: 3 }] })

Methodology: Thirty anchored questions. Dimension means are combined using explicit weights and renormalised over answered dimensions. Response coverage is reported separately; bands are withheld below 80% coverage. Empty responses produce an unavailable score. This is self-assessment support, not certification or legal advice.

import { scoreReadiness } from '@tenhaw/ai-readiness';
console.log(scoreReadiness({ answers: [{ questionId: 'strategy-1', score: 3 }] }));

## Delivery metrics

When to use: Calculate five DORA metrics and flow observations for one service from linked delivery events.

Install: npm install @tenhaw/delivery-metrics@1.0.1

CLI: npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 delivery-metrics --from-file events.json --since 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z --until 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z --json

API: computeMetrics(events, { since, until, service })

Methodology: Observed production deployments, linked commits and incidents underpin five DORA metrics. Tags and merges are excluded as deployment proxies. Missing evidence remains unavailable. Periods are half-open [since, until), timestamps require timezones, and services are computed separately. Health output is informational, with data improvement prompts and no invented composite ranking.

import { computeMetrics } from '@tenhaw/delivery-metrics';
const report = computeMetrics([], { since: '2026-10-01T00:00:00Z', until: '2026-11-01T00:00:00Z' });
console.log(report.metrics.changeFailRate); // value: null

## AI ROI and project cost

When to use: Compare low, base and high AI business-case assumptions without treating recovered staff capacity as cash by default.

Install: npm install @tenhaw/ai-roi@1.0.1

CLI: npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 roi --input roi.json --json

API: calculateRoi(input); estimateProjectCost({ stage: 'poc' })

Methodology: Monthly cash flows include adoption, explicit cash realisation, build cost, ongoing cost and discounting. Cash realisation defaults to zero in examples. Capacity hours remain separate. NPV discounts monthly flows by (1 + annual rate)^(month / 12). Payback is null if cumulative cash flow never breaks even. All cost defaults are editable assumptions, not quotes or financial advice.

import { calculateRoi } from '@tenhaw/ai-roi';
// Complete input: /examples/roi.json
const report = calculateRoi(input);
console.log(report.scenarios.base.npv);

## AI use-case register

When to use: Keep use-case ownership, value, feasibility and governance review together in a structured register.

Install: npm install @tenhaw/usecase-register@1.0.1

CLI: npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 usecases prioritise --input register.json --json

API: prioritiseUseCases({ useCases }); exportRegister(report, 'csv')

Methodology: Priority is value multiplied by feasibility, each between 0 and 5. Prohibited indicative uses are blocked; high or unknown risk requires review. Governance gates precede score ordering. Risk descriptions are indicative, not legal advice. Transparency obligations may coexist with high-risk obligations.

import { prioritiseUseCases } from '@tenhaw/usecase-register';
console.log(prioritiseUseCases({ useCases: [] }));

## Product operating model

When to use: Validate team ownership, outcome-led roadmaps, OKRs and team interactions.

Install: npm install @tenhaw/opmodel@1.0.1

CLI: npx -y tenhaw@1.0.1 opmodel validate model.json --json

API: generateOperatingModel({ teams, okrs, roadmap, interactions }); renderMermaid(report)

Methodology: Team types and interactions reference Team Topologies without affiliation. Checks identify missing ownership, outcomes and support declarations. They prompt design conversations rather than prescribe an organisation. Key-result progress is (current - baseline) / (target - baseline), supporting decreasing targets.

import { generateOperatingModel } from '@tenhaw/opmodel';
console.log(generateOperatingModel({ teams: [] }));
